messages.subject: simmer matching mechanism
messages.body_plain:
Hello,
I have two sets of arrivals  and I am trying to define a matching mechanism using simmer.

Assume that I have 10 students that arrive in a waiting list for rooms in a dormitory.

The students  arrive based on a exponential distribution.
the rooms at the dormitory also become available based on a a exponential distribution.  However, the number of rooms is smaller than the number of students and the they become available based on a smaller rate.

students have requested for 2 attributes that are the number of beds in the room and size based on the rooms characteristics.

e.g:
total_number_room = 6
room_tyep_A = 3 beds, size= 1000 sqf (there are two type A rooms)
room_type_B= 3 beds, size=700 sqf  (there is one type B room)
room_type_C = 2 beds, size= 700 sqf (there are 3 type C rooms)
room_type_D = 2 beds, size= 500 sqf (there is one type D room)

if a room becomes available and it matches the attributes a student asked for, he/she will be assigned the room. The student will stay (trap) in the waiting list otherwise so a room become available based on his/her request. However,  after a while he/she has to leave the waiting list and find a place outside of the campus.

I tried to replicate this situation using the examples available at simmer-r, however, I have got confused about defining the matching process and how I should treat the rooms in the process. I believe they should be defined in a trajectory because of the way they become available, however they are also resources that can be seized.

I appreciate it if you would help me out setting up this simulation. Thanks for your help in advance.

S.H

messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] simmer matching mechanism
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Based on your specification, I would define 1 trajectory per type of room, where you have n = #rooms * #beds/room beds. Each student goes to the specific trajectory based on their preferences, and they just try to seize a bed. I think you don't need signals for this problem. Reneging from waiting can be achieved with renege_in().

Iñaki

messages.subject: Seed changes outcome in dining philosophers
messages.subject_clean: Seed changes outcome in dining philosophers
messages.body_plain:
Hi folks.

The dining philosopher example (https://r-simmer.org/articles/simmer-08-philosophers.html) details out the importance of the fork selection policy. However, by simply changing the seed to 313 all philosophers eat spaghetti (see the corresponding screenshot when running the script with seed set to 313) with the simplistic initial fork selection policy.

So why is the selection adjustment `fork_seq$Aristotle <- rev(fork_seq$Aristotle)` necessary/justified? It could also be just a coincidence that it works because of the seed and may fail for other seeds.

Thanks & Best
Holger Brandl

messages.subject: Non-stationary Poisson Process
messages.body_plain:
I have been scouring the vignettes and reference material to understand how Simmer deals with non-stationary (or non-homogeneous) arrival processes. I have yet to see any information on (1) how to implement a non-stationary arrival process or (2) the method used to generate non-stationary arrivals.

Before I spend a day running tests or writing a personalized (and therefore inevitably inefficiency) thinning process, I wanted to see if anyone can point me in the right direction.

Thanks in advance,
David

I have yet to see any information on (1) how to implement a non-stationary arrival process or (2) the method used to generate non-stationary arrivals.

One of the strengths of simmer (in my opinion) is that the simulation engine is completely process-agnostic. You can either implement your own arrival process as an R function (inside this function, you can rely on standard R functions, other packages, call compiled code...; and also you can query the simulation time <https://r-simmer.org/reference/now.html>, the state of resources, attributes... <https://r-simmer.org/reference/index.html#section-manage-simulation-environments>) and feed it to add_generator <https://r-simmer.org/reference/add_generator.html>, or take a bunch of arrivals from any source (e.g., experimental ones) and feed them to add_dataframe <https://r-simmer.org/reference/add_dataframe.html>.

--
